value.text: Full parity-failure classification against the 2026.10.19 oracle, all verified empirically against the published 10.14 and 10.19 packages: (a) intended upstream changes: GH-1457 in 10.15 (explicit --limit binds under --no-truncate; no-truncate disables only the implicit token ceiling and the 10k row guard), GH-1465 in 10.17 (foreign principal release under warn governance emits ownership_warning:assignee_conflict in the release envelope; forced and bypass releases stay silent, strict still refuses), GH-1464 in 10.17 (successful warn-mode close returns follow_up kind complete_close_evidence with suggested_command/suggested_command_args instead of failure-shaped recovery), GH-1478 in 10.17 (240 UTF-16-unit string compaction steps back one unit to preserve surrogate pairs in JSON and TOON; no lone-surrogate escapes; the retained malformed-override refusal stays), GH-1481 in 10.18 (explicit --sort keys appear once in brief rows and projection.fields; title excluded as already present), GH-1489 in 10.18 (all-status spellings and terminal-family status filters keep the brief default; explicit --full and raw SDK full reads stay full). No upstream bug from the parity list surfaced as a divergence; upstream issues 1507 and 1509-1514 remain byte-kept quirks with no native fixes smuggled in. Native defects: none found; every failure mapped to an upstream behaviour change. Fixes: release envelope warning in mutation.rs ownership path, close follow_up receipt, list projection model (all-status brief, sort key in brief, explicit producer limit under no-truncate), pair-preserving compact_strings; golden list fixture regenerated from the 10.19 oracle with new full and full-all labels; differential and unit tests updated to the new contracts.
